The test image shows a soybean stem at a node with **white fluffy/cottony mycelial growth** — the classic hallmark of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot). The white cottony mass at the node matches perfectly with the White_Mold reference images, which show identical fluffy white growth on stems at nodes.

No other class fits: Powdery Mildew affects leaves, not stems at nodes; Pythium/Rhizoctonia/Fusarium affect roots/seedlings; Charcoal Rot shows gray discoloration without white mycelium; Diaporthe shows black pycnidia on stems.
